result.keyword: What's the best project management tool for a startup?
result.markdown:
For most startups, **Linear is the best project management tool if you're building a tech or SaaS product.** However, the best choice depends on your team's size, workflow, and whether you're managing product development, business operations, or both.

My recommendation: choose something that is easy to adopt, doesn't require a dedicated project manager, and can scale as your startup grows.

## Best project management tools for startups

![Fast growing startups are built on Linear](https://images.openai.com/static-rsc-4/piHpddRS6n9dTggcCRU3QzspXui7xfTg4qksC0xamyVTz0l5rmZLEYCGsVB7KKUouzfiOTbe-9ydzUq7UB2MFrNbZIGlaUSNjP0C8Bhd2CXnbxL2xZ05zw3USDTcATN8Ed4Fr3ygsGaA-sAB5VFRUeF1jd3BNolTylsoZGFQvpYkliFtHTL_AgaQh3gID9Z3?purpose=fullsize)

**1\. Linear**

(Best for tech startups)

- Excellent product roadmaps and sprint planning
- Fast, clean interface
- Great for engineering and product teams
- GitHub integration

**My take\:** Best if your startup is building software.

[Visit Linear](https://linear.app/)

---

![Finastra Customer Story | ClickUp™](https://images.openai.com/static-rsc-4/OXxUksa73j7hoTxbYQ6zo3pspX36GflPBLMsRWXjhfWZTJdFq6md_tXaxCCc_3Kjh0xQSrUSgXoCYi3d5TOe48r-mvzFwLplQbgf4lhsH3q_bsATt_hAcyva5qI1DtZG8OasgRxxldReZAIfURcJdNdt2Br8nPVvqn-lCO5aR2MxpFl9QAiCxibf4gzehOOb?purpose=fullsize)

**2\. ClickUp**

(Best all-in-one option)

- Tasks, projects, documents and goals
- Dashboards and automation
- Useful for marketing, sales, operations and product
- Generous free starting option

**My take\:** Best if you want one platform for the entire company.

[Visit ClickUp](https://clickup.com/)

---

![11+ Notion Project Management Templates [2023]](https://images.openai.com/static-rsc-4/7VHtPGkC6kCpTyfxJ6syWGjCLmPPVdJFM4vRKhWxKAHVNKFCJnK8BufrhGE8WjMdsBIw3Eh3SIwdS2Bv5WTuoJMH8QsCFNW2QE-rv7fk8pbCs5PhT5g5Ctc4uBcK5ky8f339ESndXQL91ic4fifvuyjJrUAIeidHGPdLFyccVwXTvr3Dy2Y3XHM8NzJD8ART?purpose=fullsize)

**3\. Notion**

- Project tracking and task databases
- Company wiki and documentation
- Meeting notes and strategic planning
- Highly customizable

**My take\:** Excellent for founders who want company knowledge and projects together.

[Visit Notion](https://www.notion.com/)

---

![Asana's Work Tracking & Project Management Features • Asana](https://images.openai.com/static-rsc-4/m19YDUwdC_b4_iZ9n9z8fSe6euf1-ZmRcXQIXRShoKd_oJ2W0DR8vK1oDjzmri5gzUiXKJRFvGVidtmiypZgR-gKbDksqI5iHbUkcYB0jKczJIWkGG_IbSGPDGHVDViKyY9Kyrza2wJkrgYRDGwZK2A5ibCNk6hoMUEoqGkVkrw5Ej_3DHbaTnJpZYSGEbXN?purpose=fullsize)

**4\. Asana**

- Clear task ownership and deadlines
- Project dependencies
- Cross-team collaboration
- Progress reporting

**My take\:** Great for startups with multiple departments.

[Visit Asana](https://asana.com/)

---

![Logiciel de gestion de projets | monday.com](https://images.openai.com/static-rsc-4/AGLC0Xsp-rKstoXsyE6UCQfot3lTpB5cGra6xvTB-1Y-qIA05m9_6HsnuIkFXzG46Gdq0IyVInVwNUGPugF02K85XBGt2B7g_m0JBT62CyuGLR87_WyvYcanfNCRIgGLOpxv6O7TSm-Ik4NJ7iGSyfd0i6QBhld455AzsGClawDFf8KDZZY7FV7QUZkaNONC?purpose=fullsize)

**5\. monday.com**

- Visual project dashboards
- Custom workflows
- Automation and reporting
- Good for operations-heavy teams

**My take\:** Great when the company starts growing and needs more structured processes.

[Visit monday.com](https://monday.com/)

## My comparison

| Tool | Best use case | Complexity |
|--------|--------|--------|
| Linear | Product & engineering | Low |
| ClickUp | Entire startup | Medium |
| Notion | Knowledge & planning | Low |
| Asana | Team coordination | Medium |
| monday.com | Business operations | Medium |


These are qualitative fit assessments, not benchmark scores.

## What I would choose

- **Pre-seed / 1–5 people\:** Notion or ClickUp.
- **Seed stage / 5–20 people\:** ClickUp or Linear + Notion.
- **Growing startup / 20–50 people\:** Asana or monday.com.
- **SaaS startup with developers\:** Linear + Notion.

One important piece of advice: don't overcomplicate project management early. Start with a simple system\:

1. Company goals and priorities.
2. Projects and milestones.
3. Tasks with clear owners.
4. Deadlines and progress tracking.
5. Weekly team review.
